name: Air Carnival
note: Coimbatore-based ATR 72 operator.

name: Air Costa
note: Vijayawada-based Embraer operator; suspended over lease payment difficulties and never returned.

name: Air Deccan
note: Relaunched Air Deccan brand of Deccan Charters (G.R. Gopinath) on UDAN routes with Beechcraft 1900D, after a scheduled commuter permit on 22 December 2017. Its Maharashtra routes stopped in early October 2018; all scheduled flights stopped 5 April 2020 (COVID) and never resumed. The original Air Deccan (2003) is a different airline that became Kingfisher Red.

name: Air Heritage
note: Heritage Aviation's UDAN service from Dehradun (Dehradun-Pithoragarh first); suspended after a 9 February 2019 in-flight door incident, then resumed about seven months later. The company now flies Uttarakhand UDAN helicopter routes.

name: Air India
renamed: Tata Air Lines to Tata Air Services / Tata Airlines (1938); Tata Airlines to Air India (1946-07-29)
note: Began as Tata's Karachi-Bombay air mail service. Absorbed Indian Airlines (codes merged February 2011) and Vistara (12 November 2024).
source_notes: dgca-traffic-report: Air India's domestic operations as printed until the Air India Group rows begin

name: Air India and Alliance Air
source_notes: dgca-traffic-report: Combined row in the route dispersal table

name: Air India Express
note: Absorbed AIX Connect (ex AirAsia India) on 1 October 2024; new brand identity and livery from 18 October 2023.

name: Air India Group
source_notes: dgca-traffic-report: Printed from January 2025; the report says it includes Air India and Air India Express

name: Air Odisha
note: Bhubaneswar-based UDAN operator (Beechcraft 1900D, Cessna 208). Stopped flying in early October 2018 (last Jharsuguda flight 6 October 2018); AAI cancelled its UDAN award in November 2018.

name: Air Pegasus
note: Bengaluru-based ATR 72 operator.

name: Air Taxi
source_notes: dgca-operating-stats: DGCA's row name; the file does not name an operator.

name: AIX Connect
note: Renamed after Tata Sons bought out AirAsia Bhd's stake; its I5 code was retired when it merged into Air India Express.
source_notes: dgca-operating-stats: DGCA lists it as Air Asia to 2023 and as AIX Connect in 2024. A separate operator from Air India Express in these files.; dgca-traffic-report: Printed as Air Asia, later AIX Connect

name: Akasa Air
note: First flight Mumbai-Ahmedabad.

name: Alliance Air
renamed: Alliance Air to Air India Regional (brand) (2011); Air India Regional to Alliance Air (2022-04-15)
note: Indian Airlines subsidiary, then Air India's; separated from Air India before privatisation and has operated independently since 15 April 2022. Flies ATR 72/42 and Dornier 228 turboprops on regional and UDAN routes.

name: Blue Dart Aviation
note: Cargo airline of Blue Dart Express (DHL group).

name: Deccan Air
note: Very likely the same operator as the relaunched Air Deccan (Deccan Charters). DGCA's 2017 'Deccan Air' file says it 'started its operations from the month of December 2017', the month Air Deccan got its scheduled commuter permit (22 Dec) and flew its first flight (23 Dec). No other 'Deccan' scheduled operator started then.
source_notes: dgca-operating-stats: Listed for 2017 and 2018. Kept apart from Air Deccan (2020, 2021) because DGCA's files do not say they are one operator.

name: Fly91
note: Goa-based ATR 72-600 operator; reuses Indian Airlines' old IC code.

name: flybig
note: Promoted by Big Charter Pvt Ltd (no link to Deccan Charters found). ATR flights suspended November 2023 when lessors repossessed aircraft; Twin Otters kept flying until about October 2025; formally ceased when its AOC expired 13 December 2025.

name: Go First
note: Suspended all flights from 3 May 2023 and filed for insolvency on 2 May 2023; never resumed. NCLT New Delhi ordered liquidation on 20 January 2025.
source_notes: dgca-operating-stats: DGCA's files keep the name Go Air throughout.; dgca-traffic-report: Printed as Go Air until 2021

name: Indian Airlines
note: Companies amalgamated into NACIL (later Air India Ltd) effective 27 August 2007, but flew under its own IC code, and DGCA reported it separately, until the single AI code took over on 27 February 2011.
source_notes: dgca-operating-stats: Reported apart from Air India until 2011.

name: IndiaOne Air
note: Bhubaneswar-based Cessna Caravan operator on UDAN routes; first scheduled flight Bhubaneswar-Jeypore.

name: IndiGo
note: First service New Delhi-Imphal via Guwahati.

name: Jet Airways
note: All flights suspended 17 April 2019; a 2022 AOC renewal under Jalan-Kalrock never led to flights. Supreme Court ordered liquidation on 7 November 2024.
source_notes: dgca-operating-stats: DGCA's 2019 file: operations suspended from 18 April 2019.

name: JetLite
renamed: Air Sahara to JetLite (2007-04-16); JetLite to JetKonnect (brand) (2012-03-25)
note: Ex Sahara Airlines / Air Sahara, bought by Jet Airways in April 2007. The JetLite brand ended on 25 March 2012 when its flights moved under Jet Airways' JetKonnect brand, but the company Jet Lite (India) Ltd kept reporting to DGCA separately and grounded with its parent on 17 April 2019.

name: Kingfisher Airlines
note: Flights stopped around 30 September/1 October 2012 amid an employee strike; DGCA suspended its permit from 20 October 2012; slots and flying rights withdrawn February 2013. It had absorbed Air Deccan (rebranded Simplifly Deccan, then Kingfisher Red) after 2007-08.

name: MDLR Airlines
note: Gurgaon-based airline of the MDLR group.

name: Paramount Airways
note: Chennai-hub Embraer 170/190 operator with all business-class cabins; fleet grounded by lessors from March 2010, a planned November 2010 restart never happened.

name: Pawan Hans
renamed: Helicopter Corporation of India to Pawan Hans (1986-08)
note: State-owned helicopter operator (operations from 1 November 1985). First helicopter operator to get a Scheduled Commuter Operator permit; runs UDAN helicopter routes (Uttarakhand from July 2020). Fixed-wing only via the Jal Hans seaplane (Andamans, from 27 Dec 2010).

name: Quikjet Cargo
note: Bengaluru-based freighter operator.

name: SpiceJet
note: Same company that flew as ModiLuft until 1996; relaunched as low-cost SpiceJet after Ajay Singh's 2004 acquisition.

name: Star Air
note: Ghodawat group airline flying Embraer ERJ 145 and E175 jets on regional and UDAN routes; first flight Bengaluru-Hubballi.

name: TruJet
note: Operated by Turbo Megha Airways from Hyderabad with ATR 72s; ceased over a financial crisis.

name: Vistara
note: Last Vistara-coded flights operated 11 November 2024; from 12 November its flights carry Air India AI 2xxx numbers.

name: Zoom Air
note: Zexus Air Services, branded Zoom Air and later Zooom, flying CRJ200s. DGCA suspended its permit in July 2018; flights restarted 31 January 2024 (Delhi-Ayodhya) after an AOC renewal on 14 September 2023, then stopped again 29 June 2024.
